title: Claude Code settings payload holding only hooks
description: The shape of a hooks-only Claude Code settings object, the payload a session host passes to `claude --settings <json>`. Transcribed from the Claude Code hooks reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, retrieved 2026-10-18, naming releases up to 2.1.299): § Configuration (three levels of nesting: hook event, matcher group, hook handler), § Matcher patterns (the event table and the `matcher` field on the group), § Hook handler fields and § Command hook fields (`type`, `command`, `async`), and § Run hooks in the background. It is written from the documentation, not from lore's payload builder, so a payload that fails it is a payload Claude Code may reject or misread; a mismatch between this file and the documentation is reported, not patched to fit a builder. Validators read only the keywords used here: type, const, enum, required, properties, additionalProperties, propertyNames, items, minItems, minLength, minProperties, $ref into $defs.
$comment: Deliberately narrower than the documentation in three places. The root holds only `hooks`: any other key would ride the same settings source and could shadow the person's own settings. Handlers are command handlers only. A command handler carries only `type`, `command` and `async`; the other documented command-hook fields are excluded because each changes what a lifecycle hook may do: `asyncRewake` keeps the hook timeout armed and wakes the model on exit 2, `statusMessage` draws a spinner near the composer the screen fallback reads, `timeout` is not enforced on async hooks, and `if`, `args`, `shell` and `onFailure` change when or how the command runs.

hooks.description: Maps a hook event name to its matcher groups. Event names are the documented set (hooks reference, § Hook lifecycle and § Matcher patterns).

matcher_group.description: One matcher group: an optional `matcher` filtering when the group fires, and the handlers that run when it matches. The matcher sits on the group, never on a handler. For tool events it is tested against the tool name; a value of only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,` and `|` is an exact list of names, and anything else is an unanchored JavaScript regular expression. Omitted, empty or `*` matches every occurrence; on an event without matcher support (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PostToolBatch and others) the field is ignored.

command_handler.description: A command hook handler. `command` is a shell command run with `sh -c` on macOS and Linux, receiving the event's JSON on stdin. `async: true` runs it in the background without blocking; an async hook cannot block or control Claude, Claude Code does not enforce a timeout on it, and JSON it prints is delivered to Claude on the next turn.
